findings.title: remove_member deletes join rows with delete_all, skipping callbacks and user_count maintenance
findings.body: `group.users.delete(user_id)` goes through the `has_many :users, through: :group_users` association. For a `has_many :through` association without a `:dependent` option, `delete` removes the join rows with `delete_all`, so no `GroupUser` is instantiated and no ActiveRecord callbacks / counter-cache updates run. Consequences: the cached `groups.user_count` column (exposed by `BasicGroupSerializer` and used by the admin group list and group index) is never decremented and drifts permanently, and any `GroupUser` destroy-time bookkeeping (e.g. clearing `primary_group`/badge title that was granted by the group) is skipped. The removal should go through the model API that destroys the join record, e.g. `group.remove(user)` or `group.group_users.where(user_id: user_id).destroy_all`. Additionally, passing an id that is not a member makes the association call `find(id)` and raise `ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound`, turning a no-op removal into a 404 instead of a clean response.

findings.title: create ignores alias_level sent by the client
findings.body: `create` only assigns `name` and `visible`, but the client (`Discourse.Group#asJSON`, used by `create()`) always sends `alias_level` as well. A group created with a non-default alias level in the admin UI is silently saved with the default level, and the UI then shows the value the admin picked, so the discrepancy is invisible until a page reload. `update` does assign `alias_level`; `create` should do the same. Note also that this change switches the create/update payload from nested `group[...]` params to flat params and drops support for `usernames`, which breaks any existing API client of `POST/PUT /admin/groups`.

findings.title: Removal of the PATCH membership endpoint makes old PATCH requests silently destructive
findings.body: The `update_patch` branch (incremental `changes: {add:, delete:}` membership edits) was deleted, but `resources :groups` still routes PATCH to `update`. A client still issuing `PATCH /admin/groups/:id` with `changes` now gets HTTP 200 while the membership changes are silently discarded, and because `update` unconditionally executes `group.visible = params[:visible] == "true"`, the absent `visible` param flips the group to not visible. Old callers therefore both lose their intended effect and mutate unrelated state while being told everything succeeded. Either keep handling `changes` (or reject PATCH explicitly) and only assign `visible` when the param is present.

findings.title: members endpoint does not validate limit/offset
findings.body: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i` are passed straight to `.limit()/.offset()`. A request with `?offset=-1` or `?limit=-1` produces `OFFSET -1` / `LIMIT -1`, which PostgreSQL rejects (`ERROR: OFFSET must not be negative`), turning a bad query string into a 500. There is also no upper bound on `limit`, so `?limit=1000000` on a large automatic group (e.g. trust_level_0) will serialize every member in one unauthenticated-reachable request, an easy way to burn server CPU/memory. Clamp both values (e.g. `limit` to 1..100, `offset` to >= 0) server-side; the JS clamping in `Discourse.Group#findMembers` protects nothing against direct requests.

findings.title: GET /groups/:name/members response shape changed from array to object
findings.body: The endpoint previously rendered a bare JSON array of serialized users (`render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)`); it now returns `{"members": [...], "meta": {...}}`. This is an unversioned, breaking change for any external API consumer or plugin that reads `/groups/:name/members.json` as an array (they will now see an object and silently iterate nothing). If the break is intentional it should at least be called out in the PR description/changelog; otherwise consider keeping the array for non-paginated requests.

findings.title: Public group members page now silently truncated to 50 members
findings.body: `model.findMembers()` requests the default page (limit 50, offset 0) and `discourse/templates/group/members.hbs` renders only `members` with no pagination controls. Previously non-automatic groups returned all members from this endpoint, so a group with more than 50 members now shows only the first 50 with no way for a user to reach the rest. Either add next/previous controls (as done in the admin template) or load all pages for this route.

findings.title: totalPages off by one produces a reachable empty page
findings.body: `totalPages` is `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`, which over-counts whenever `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`: with 100 members and limit 50 it reports 3 pages even though only 2 contain data. Combined with `next`, which sets `offset = Math.min(offset + limit, user_count)`, an admin can page to `offset == user_count` and see "3/3" with an empty member list (and `previous` then lands on a non page-aligned offset). Use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` and advance the offset in whole pages.

findings.title: Add/remove member failures are swallowed with no user feedback
findings.body: `addMembers` and `removeMember` call into `Discourse.Group#addMembers` / `#removeMember`, neither of which attach a rejection handler. If the server responds 422 (e.g. `can_not_modify_automatic`) or 404/500 (see the RecordNotFound path in `Admin::GroupsController#remove_member`), the promise rejects silently: the member list is not refreshed and the admin gets no indication the operation failed. Add an error handler that surfaces the message (as `save`/`destroy` in this controller already do). The `// TODO: should clear the input` note is related: because `usernames` is never reset, clicking Add again re-sends the same list.

findings.title: add_members assumes usernames is a String and silently ignores unknown users
findings.body: `usernames.split(",")` raises `NoMethodError` (HTTP 500) if the parameter arrives as an array (`usernames[]=a&usernames[]=b`), which is a natural shape for API clients. Also, usernames that do not resolve to a `User` are skipped and the action still returns `success_json`, so an admin who mistypes a username sees a successful save and no member added, with no error reported. Normalize the parameter (`Array(usernames).join(",").split(",")` or similar) and report unknown usernames back to the caller.

findings.title: No spec for the rewritten members endpoint
findings.body: `GroupsController#members` changed substantially in this PR (new `{members:, meta:}` envelope, new default limit of 50 applied to all groups instead of automatic groups only, `total` computed with a separate count query), but the only spec touched is `spec/controllers/admin/groups_controller_spec.rb`. There is no test asserting the new response structure, that `limit`/`offset` are honoured and echoed in `meta`, or that `total` reflects the full member count — so the response-shape break and any future regression in pagination would go unnoticed.

findings.title: remove_member spec uses a verb the route does not support
findings.body: The test issues `xhr :put, :remove_member`, but `config/routes.rb` only declares `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`. Controller specs dispatch directly to the action, so the test passes even though a real PUT to `/admin/groups/:group_id/members` would be handled by `add_members`, not `remove_member`. The automatic-group guard for the DELETE path is therefore not actually covered; use `xhr :delete, :remove_member` as the other spec in the same context does.

findings.title: Specs depend on hardcoded group id 1 being an automatic group
findings.body: The new `.update` spec (`id: 1`) and the `.add_members` / `.remove_member` automatic-group specs (`group_id: 1`) rely on seeded data where group id 1 happens to exist and be automatic, and `.update` then calls `Group.find(1)`. If seeds change or the test database is built differently, these raise `RecordNotFound` rather than fail meaningfully, and nothing in the spec documents the assumption. Fabricate an automatic group explicitly (`Fabricate(:group, automatic: true)`) as the `.destroy` spec does.
